21:1.sourceText: Ἀναβλέψας δὲ εἶδεν τοὺς βάλλοντας εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον τὰ δῶρα αὐτῶν πλουσίους.
21:1.targetText: And having looked up, He saw those who cast their gifts into the treasury—rich men,

groups.note: Actual masculine plural rich adjective identifies the rich people. English spells out rich men; no independently written Greek man noun is invented.

21:2.sourceText: εἶδεν δέ τινα χήραν πενιχρὰν βάλλουσαν ἐκεῖ λεπτὰ δύο,
21:2.targetText: and He also saw a certain poor widow casting two mites there,

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly has καί after δέ. Pinned N1904 lacks that additional additive particle.

21:3.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν Ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα αὕτη ἡ πτωχὴ πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν·
21:3.targetText: and He said, “Truly I say to you that this poor widow cast in more than all;

groups.note: Actual ἔβαλεν is the casting predicate, rendered with the English phrasal cast in. No separately printed Greek in preposition or prefixed casting form is claimed.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

21:4.sourceText: πάντες γὰρ οὗτοι ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον εἰς τὰ δῶρα, αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τοῦ ὑστερήματος αὐτῆς πάντα τὸν βίον ὃν εἶχεν ἔβαλεν.
21:4.targetText: for all these out of their superabundance cast into the gifts to God, but this one out of her want, all the living that she had, cast in.”

groups.note: Actual ἐκ plus article and substantival abounding participle names the surplus resources. English nominalizes that same phrase as out of superabundance; no separate Greek superabundance noun is invented.
Actual dative αὐτοῖς supplies the people for whom the resources abound. English renders those same surplus-owners as their; no genitive Greek form or different owner is claimed.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly adds τοῦ θεοῦ with the gifts, represented as to God in English. Pinned N1904 prints no God noun or such recipient/possessor phrase there.

21:5.sourceText: Καί τινων λεγόντων περὶ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, ὅτι λίθοις καλοῖς καὶ ἀναθήμασιν κεκόσμηται, εἶπεν
21:5.targetText: And [as] some were speaking about the temple, that it has been adorned with good stones and devoted things, He said,

groups.note: Actual genitive-absolute speaking participle supplies a temporal frame. English renders it as [as] and finite were speaking; no independently written Greek as conjunction or finite speaking form is claimed.

21:6.sourceText: Ταῦτα ἃ θεωρεῖτε, ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται λίθος ἐπὶ λίθῳ ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται.
21:6.targetText: “These things that you behold—days will come in which there will not be left a stone on a stone that will not be thrown down.”

21:7.sourceText: ἐπηρώτησαν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε, πότε οὖν ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα γίνεσθαι;
21:7.targetText: And they questioned Him, saying, “Teacher, when, then, will these things be? And what [is] the sign when these things may be about to happen?”

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the what-is-the-sign nominal question. Pinned N1904 prints no separate be verb in that second question.

21:8.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Βλέπετε μὴ πλανηθῆτε· πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες Ἐγώ εἰμι, καί Ὁ καιρὸς ἤγγικεν· μὴ πορευθῆτε ὀπίσω αὐτῶν.
21:8.targetText: And He said, “See—you may not be led astray, for many will come in My Name, saying, I am [He], and the time has come near; do not then go on after them;

groups.note: Actual πορευθῆτε is the aorist subjunctive movement form in the negative prohibition. English uses do ... go on; no imperative source analysis or separate Greek auxiliary verb is invented.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a predicate personal pronoun after I am. Pinned N1904 prints no independent He pronoun there.
TR explicitly includes οὖν in the final prohibition. Pinned N1904 lacks that additional inference particle.

21:9.sourceText: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκαταστασίας, μὴ πτοηθῆτε· δεῖ γὰρ ταῦτα γενέσθαι πρῶτον, ἀλλ’ οὐκ εὐθέως τὸ τέλος.
21:9.targetText: and when you may hear of wars and uprisings, do not be terrified, for it is necessary for these things to happen first, but the end [is] not immediately.”

groups.note: Actual accusative wars is the hearing object. English uses hear of wars; no Greek genitive or independent of preposition is claimed.

Actual ἀκαταστασία names disorder, riot or rebellion, explicitly attested at Luke21:9 by the primary Mounce entry. English uprisings retains that unrest head rather than substituting a different Greek war noun.
Actual accusative ταῦτα is subject of the happening infinitive. English introduces that same infinitival subject with for; no independently printed Greek for preposition is invented.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in the end-not-immediately nominal statement. N1904 prints no be verb in that final clause.

21:10.sourceText: Τότε ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ἐγερθήσεται ἔθνος ἐπ’ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν,
21:10.targetText: Then He said to them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom,

groups.note: Actual Ἐγερθήσεται is future passive, used for the rising event. English renders it with intransitive will rise; no active Greek form or separately named external raiser is invented.

21:11.sourceText: σεισμοί τε μεγάλοι καὶ κατὰ τόπους λοιμοὶ καὶ λιμοὶ ἔσονται, φόβητρά τε καὶ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἔσται.
21:11.targetText: also great shakings, and there will be famines and pestilences in every place; also there will be fearful things and great signs from the sky;

groups.note: Actual distributive κατὰ τόπους is the according-to-places phrase. English expands that distributive location to in every place, without an independently printed Greek every quantifier.

review.note: N1904 orders pestilences before famines, while TR and LSV order famines before pestilences. Actual noun heads remain paired to their own English meanings rather than mechanical list positions.

21:12.sourceText: πρὸ δὲ τούτων πάντων ἐπιβαλοῦσιν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν καὶ διώξουσιν, παραδιδόντες εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ φυλακάς, ἀπαγομένους ἐπὶ βασιλεῖς καὶ ἡγεμόνας ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου·
21:12.targetText: and before all these, they will lay on you their hands, and persecute, delivering up to synagogues and prisons, being brought before kings and governors for My Name’s sake;

groups.note: Actual genitive article/name phrase is rendered with the English possessive Name’s in the for-name’s-sake construction; no independent Greek possessive suffix or different name owner is invented.

21:13.targetText: and it will become to you for a testimony.

groups.note: Actual ἀποβήσεται is the becoming/resulting/turning-out predicate. The primary Mounce ἀποβαίνω entry explicitly attests that outcome sense at Luke21:13; no printed γίνομαι lemma or physical disembarking claim is substituted.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly includes δέ after the outcome predicate. Pinned N1904 prints no corresponding connective in this verse.

21:14.sourceText: θέτε οὖν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν μὴ προμελετᾶν ἀπολογηθῆναι·
21:14.targetText: Settle, then, to your hearts, not to meditate beforehand to reply,

groups.note: Actual ἐν with the hearts phrase is locative; TR instead has εἰς. English uses to your hearts with settle. The complete inner-location phrase is paired without inventing a directional N1904 preposition.

21:15.sourceText: ἐγὼ γὰρ δώσω ὑμῖν στόμα καὶ σοφίαν, ᾗ οὐ δυνήσονται ἀντιστῆναι ἢ ἀντειπεῖν ἅπαντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι ὑμῖν.
21:15.targetText: for I will give to you a mouth and wisdom that all your opposers will not be able to refute or resist.

groups.note: Actual dative ὑμῖν identifies the people being opposed. English renders that same relation as your opposers; no Greek genitive ownership form or different opposed party is claimed.

review.note: N1904 orders resist before contradict/refute; TR and LSV reverse those two predicates. Each actual predicate is linked to its own English head, with the different written order retained.

21:16.sourceText: παραδοθήσεσθε δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ γονέων καὶ ἀδελφῶν καὶ συγγενῶν καὶ φίλων, καὶ θανατώσουσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν,
21:16.targetText: And you will be delivered up also by parents, and brothers, and relatives, and friends, and they will put [some] of you to death;

groups.note: Actual ἐξ ὑμῶν is the partitive from-among-you phrase. English spells out the implied partitive members as [some] of you; no independently printed Greek some pronoun is invented.

21:17.sourceText: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.
21:17.targetText: and you will be hated by all because of My Name—

21:18.sourceText: καὶ θρὶξ ἐκ τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν οὐ μὴ ἀπόληται·
21:18.targetText: and a hair out of your head will not perish;

groups.note: Actual ἀπόληται is aorist subjunctive with the emphatic οὐ μή negation. English uses will not perish; the actual subjunctive construction is retained rather than relabeled as a future indicative.

21:19.sourceText: ἐν τῇ ὑπομονῇ ὑμῶν κτήσεσθε τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.
21:19.targetText: in your patience possess your souls.

groups.note: Actual κτήσεσθε is future middle indicative, whereas TR has imperative κτήσασθε. English uses the possess instruction; the actual future form and acquire/possess lemma remain visible without an imperative N1904 analysis.

21:20.sourceText: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε κυκλουμένην ὑπὸ στρατοπέδων Ἱερουσαλήμ, τότε γνῶτε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ ἐρήμωσις αὐτῆς.
21:20.targetText: And when you may see Jerusalem surrounded by encampments, then know that her desolation has come near;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

21:21.sourceText: τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη, καὶ οἱ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς ἐκχωρείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἐν ταῖς χώραις μὴ εἰσερχέσθωσαν εἰς αὐτήν,
21:21.targetText: then those in Judea, let them flee to the mountains; and those in her midst, let them depart out; and those in the countries, do not let them come in to her;

groups.note: Actual εἰσερχέσθωσαν is a third-person plural imperative, negated by μή. English uses do not let them come in to realize that jussive; no separately written second-person forbidding or allowing verb is claimed.

21:22.sourceText: ὅτι ἡμέραι ἐκδικήσεως αὗταί εἰσιν τοῦ πλησθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα.
21:22.targetText: because these are days of vengeance, to fulfill all things that have been written.

groups.note: Actual articular passive πλησθῆναι is from πίμπλημι, whose fulfilled/completed sense at Luke21:22 is expressly attested in the primary Mounce entry. TR instead has πληρωθῆναι from πληρόω. English makes the same fulfillment predicate active to fulfill, retaining the written things as affected content; no different Greek lemma, active source form or independently written agent is substituted.

21:23.sourceText: οὐαὶ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις· ἔσται γὰρ ἀνάγκη μεγάλη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὀργὴ τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ,
21:23.targetText: And woe to those with child, and to those giving suck, in those days; for there will be great distress on the land, and wrath on this people;

groups.note: Actual feminine dative article plus in-womb-having idiom identifies the pregnant people. English renders the complete pregnancy phrase as to those with child; no independently printed Greek child noun is invented.
Actual dative people noun gives the group affected by wrath. English uses on this people; TR additionally prints ἐν, but no separate N1904 preposition is claimed.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly adds δέ after woe. Pinned N1904 begins directly with οὐαί without an additional connective.

21:24.sourceText: καὶ πεσοῦνται στόματι μαχαίρης καὶ αἰχμαλωτισθήσονται εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πάντα, καὶ Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἔσται πατουμένη ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν, ἄχρι οὗ πληρωθῶσιν καιροὶ ἐθνῶν.
21:24.targetText: and they will fall by the mouth of the sword, and will be led captive to all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trodden down by nations, until the times of nations be fulfilled.

groups.note: Actual αἰχμαλωτισθήσονται is the future passive taking-captive predicate. English spells out the same captivity action as will be led captive; no independently written Greek lead verb is claimed.

21:25.sourceText: Καὶ ἔσονται σημεῖα ἐν ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ καὶ ἄστροις, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς συνοχὴ ἐθνῶν ἐν ἀπορίᾳ ἤχους θαλάσσης καὶ σάλου,
21:25.targetText: And there will be signs in sun, and moon, and stars, and on the earth distress of nations with perplexity, sea and wave roaring;

groups.note: Actual ἤχους is a genitive noise/roar noun with the sea/wave genitives; TR instead prints roaring participle ἠχούσης. English turns that complete nominal roar-of-sea-and-wave constituent into sea and wave roaring; no verbal ἠχέω form or different written case is invented for N1904.

21:26.sourceText: ἀποψυχόντων ἀνθρώπων ἀπὸ φόβου καὶ προσδοκίας τῶν ἐπερχομένων τῇ οἰκουμένῃ· αἱ γὰρ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.
21:26.targetText: men fainting at heart from fear, and expectation of the things coming on the world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

groups.note: Actual ἀποψυχόντων is the fainting/expiring predicate. English uses the idiom fainting at heart; no independently printed Greek heart noun or added claim about a physiological mechanism is invented.

21:27.sourceText: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλῃ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς.
21:27.targetText: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud, with power and much glory;

21:28.sourceText: ἀρχομένων δὲ τούτων γίνεσθαι ἀνακύψατε καὶ ἐπάρατε τὰς κεφαλὰς ὑμῶν, διότι ἐγγίζει ἡ ἀπολύτρωσις ὑμῶν.
21:28.targetText: and these things beginning to happen, bend yourselves back, and lift up your heads, because your redemption draws near.”

groups.note: Actual ἀνακύψατε is the straighten/raise-oneself-up imperative, attested by the primary Mounce entry. English expresses the same upright-posture action as bend yourselves back; no independent Greek reflexive pronoun or separate back adverb is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

21:29.sourceText: Καὶ εἶπεν παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς Ἴδετε τὴν συκῆν καὶ πάντα τὰ δένδρα·
21:29.targetText: And He spoke an allegory to them: “See the fig tree, and all the trees,

21:30.sourceText: ὅταν προβάλωσιν ἤδη, βλέποντες ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤδη ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·
21:30.targetText: when they may now cast forth, having seen, of yourselves you know that now the summer is near;

groups.note: Actual βλέποντες is a present seeing participle. English uses having seen; no aorist or perfect Greek participle is substituted.

21:31.sourceText: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ.
21:31.targetText: so also you, when you may see these things happening, you know that the Kingdom of God is near;

21:32.sourceText: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
21:32.targetText: truly I say to you, this generation may not pass away until all may have come to pass;

groups.note: Actual ἂν γένηται is the particle plus aorist subjunctive becoming/happening form in the until construction. English uses modal-perfect may have come to pass; no perfect or future-perfect Greek form is claimed.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ὅτι introduces the stated declaration. English uses the speech boundary without a separate that word.

21:33.sourceText: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρελεύσονται.
21:33.targetText: the sky and the earth will pass away, but My words may not pass away.

groups.note: Actual second παρελεύσονται is future middle indicative with οὐ μή, while TR has subjunctive παρέλθωσιν. English uses may not pass away; the pinned future form remains distinct from the TR subjunctive.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

21:34.sourceText: Προσέχετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς μή ποτε βαρηθῶσιν ὑμῶν αἱ καρδίαι ἐν κραιπάλῃ καὶ μέθῃ καὶ μερίμναις βιωτικαῖς, καὶ ἐπιστῇ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς αἰφνίδιος ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη
21:34.targetText: And take heed to yourselves lest your hearts may be weighed down with carousing, and drunkenness, and anxieties of life, and suddenly that day may come on you,

groups.note: Actual βιωτικαῖς is the life-related adjective qualifying anxieties. English renders that qualifier as of life; no separately written Greek life noun or genitive form is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

21:35.sourceText: ὡς παγίς· ἐπεισελεύσεται γὰρ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.
21:35.targetText: for it will come as a snare on all those dwelling on the face of all the earth,

review.note: The pinned N1904 punctuation attaches opening ὡς παγίς as a snare to the preceding day clause, then separates the following it-will-come statement. LSV instead places the same simile inside its verse35 it-will-come clause. All actual words retain their raw21:35 anchors; no manuscript punctuation claim or changed original verse text is invented.

21:36.sourceText: ἀγρυπνεῖτε δὲ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ δεόμενοι ἵνα κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, καὶ σταθῆναι ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
21:36.targetText: watch, then, in every season, praying that you may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that are about to come to pass, and to stand before the Son of Man.”

unmappedSource.reason: Actual δέ is the continuative/adversative connector, whereas TR has inferential οὖν, followed by English then. The distinct written connective is not silently relabeled.

Actual κατισχύσητε is the active prevail/be-strong-enough predicate. TR instead prints passive καταξιωθῆτε be-accounted-worthy, followed by English. Those different lexical and voice heads are kept explicit rather than equating strength with worthiness.

unmappedTarget.reason: English follows TR οὖν then/therefore, where pinned N1904 has δέ.
English follows TR καταξιωθῆτε, not the actual N1904 prevail/be-strong-enough verb κατισχύσητε. No account-worthy lemma or passive form is invented in the pinned source.

21:37.sourceText: Ἦν δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων, τὰς δὲ νύκτας ἐξερχόμενος ηὐλίζετο εἰς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν.
21:37.targetText: And He was teaching in the temple during the days, and during the nights, going forth, He was lodging at [that] called the Mount of Olives;

groups.note: Actual accusative plural days expresses the temporal span. English uses during the days, without an independently written Greek during preposition.
Actual accusative plural nights expresses the temporal span. English uses during the nights; no independent Greek during word is claimed.
Actual εἰς with the mount phrase gives the lodging destination/site. English renders that whole governed place phrase with at; no different Greek ἐν preposition is substituted.

21:38.sourceText: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ὤρθριζεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.
21:38.targetText: and all the people were coming early to Him in the temple to hear Him.

groups.note: Actual ὤρθριζεν is singular imperfect with the collective people subject. The primary Mounce ὀρθρίζω entry attests coming with dawn at Luke21:38; English were coming early preserves that one morning-arrival predicate without a separately written coming verb or plural Greek form.
